newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TEN YEARS AFTER "HAND OF GOD", MARADONA PRAISES ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TEN YEARS AFTER "HAND OF GOD", MARADONA PRAISES ENGLAND.

text.p: The England football team's Euro '96 performances won the approval of Diego Maradona on Sunday.
The former Argentinian captain was visiting Battersea Park in London for an international youth competition.
Speaking through an interpreter he said that the new look England were a better "playing team" than the sides he faced in the 1980s.
The diminutive player, who virtually single-handedly won the 1986 World Cup for Argentina, said the England team now mixed real skill with their traditional physical presence.
Maradona, wearing wrap-around sun-glasses, jeans and a T-shirt, then left the shelter of a portable media centre to watch an Argentinian youth team play China in a four-a-side competition.
On his way, the man who scored the infamous "hand of God" goal against England 10 years ago, was mobbed by dozens of journalists from around the world as well as players in the competition.
The Puma World Junior football finals have 48 teams from 32 different countries competing in the under-14s and under-16s tournament.

After the game, Maradona, who is spending just 36 hours in Britain before visiting a doctor in Spain and returning to Argentina, showed his ball skills to the crowds by briefly juggling a football, catching it on his head and then flicking it high into the air with his heel.
He then held a brief and chaotic news conference at which he spoke through an interpreter.
He sympathised with the plight of Tony Adams, the former England captain, who on Saturday admitted his alcohol problem.

He paid tribute to English football and said it was now joining the world's "leading league". He said that despite his age - he is now in his mid 30s and overweight - he would like to play football in England.
But inevitably, most interest focused on his infamous goal scored with his hand against England in Mexico 10 years ago.

Asked if he regretted the incident, Maradona shrugged philosophically and said: "I have a few regrets but now is not the time to discuss all the regrets I have had. If we talk we will not change anything."
Yards from the press tent where Maradona was speaking stood the Rudi Voller, a member of the German team which beat Maradona's Argentina in the World Cup final in Italy in 1990.
Despite being ignored by the press, Voller was magnanimous.
"It is normal because Maradona is the greatest player in the world. I don't mind it at all."
